title: Gordon Brown 'attended exorcism to help Raith Rovers sign player' while chancellor
excerpt: Ex-Scotland manager claims former prime minister set up meeting with defender Marvin Andrews at church where pastor was ‘casting out demons’
content:
Gordon Brown, the former prime minister, attended an “exorcism” in an effort to help Raith Rovers sign a player, ex-Scotland manager Craig Levein has claimed.

Levein explained how Brown, a lifelong Raith fan, arranged a meeting in 2006 with Marvin Andrews at the Zion Praise Centre in Kirkcaldy, which was run by the Trinidad and Tobago defender’s spiritual mentor, Pastor Joe Nwokoye.

Andrews, a devout Christian, had previously played for Raith between 1997 and 2000 but was without a club at the time after being released by Rangers.

Levein told the Under The Cosh podcast that Brown, who was chancellor at the time, had phoned him telling him to come to a car park in Kirkcaldy.

“Next minute, there’s three Range Rovers that come tearing into the car park,” Levein said. “The lights are going and the sirens and I’m thinking, ‘What the f---?!’

“The window comes down and it’s Gordon.

“He says, ‘Right, jump in my car; we are going down to see Marvin’, who’s working that evening in the church.”

Levein added: “I’d chosen an evening to go along with Gordon Brown to meet Pastor Joe when they were casting out demons.

“The guys go up on the stage and Pastor Joe gets his hand on their head here and there is a whole lot of wailing noises going on and he shoves them down and they fall backwards.

“I am sitting there going, ‘What the f---’s going on?’ I’m there to meet Marvin and there are people falling about all over and there is six people lying on the ground.

“It was the most bizarre evening I have ever had.”

Andrews duly rejoined Raith, saying afterwards: “I’m delighted to be back at Stark’s Park but I’m not here because of what Gordon Brown said – I’m here because of what God said.”

Andrews, who won the Scottish Premiership with Rangers in 2005, became a full-time Christian preacher after retiring from the game and conducts weddings for football fans. He is now 50 years old.

In 2017, he offered to exorcise a house where five nannies quit in a year over fears it was haunted.

At the time, he said: “There are different types of spirits, but in my experience anything problematic is usually linked to Satan.

“It’s the devil you are dealing with. In this case the spirit is obstructive so it is a problem.”

Representatives of Gordon Brown have been contacted for comment.
